Unpopular

/uhn-POP-yuh-ler/ - the stress falls on POP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unpopular means disliked by most people.

Liver-and-onions day stayed stubbornly on the menu, unpopular with every crew the galley ever fed.

Worked Example

The library's decision to retire the wooden card index was unpopular in a way the trustees had not imagined: within a week, four hundred patrons had filled the guest book with complaints, alumni mailed in their old index cards like sympathy notes, and the Friends of the Library voted to hold their centennial gala somewhere else. Nobody defended the change at any counter in town.

Unpopular measures the crowd, not the merits: disliked by most people, full stop. Retiring the card index may even have been overdue — plenty of unpopular decisions are right, and plenty of popular ones age badly. The word simply counts the noes; whether the noes are wise is a different question entirely.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

disliked: Disliked is the plain, everyday report that people don't care for a thing — one person can dislike it, or a few. Unpopular scales that up and counts the room: most people are against it. Every unpopular rule is disliked by someone; a thing disliked by two grumps is not yet unpopular.

unwelcome: Unwelcome describes the reception a thing gets when it shows up — met with resistance at the door, whether people like it or not. A beloved cousin arriving mid-move is unwelcome; a rule is unpopular only once most people have decided against it. Unwelcome is about the arrival; unpopular is about the count.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

beloved: held in wide and warm affection

cherished: guarded as something precious

Where it sits · how strongly people turn against it — unfashionable → unpopular → despised

unfashionable vs. unpopular: Unfashionable only means the style-setters have moved on; plenty of unfashionable things are quietly loved. Unpopular counts actual noes.

despised vs. unpopular: Despised goes past unpopular: the unpopular rule collects grumbles and petitions, while the despised one collects genuine hatred — people don't just vote against it, they loathe it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — un-

Prefix — un-: not

Root — popul

Root — popul: the people

Suffix — -ar

Suffix — -ar: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Un- (not) + popul (the people, from Latin populus) + -ar (relating to) = not of the people. Latin popularis meant 'belonging to the people'; popular things have the crowd with them, and the un- simply moves the crowd to the other side of the question.

Use the root in a new word: population

Word Choice

plain / statistical

Unpopular is arithmetic: most people dislike the thing. It passes no judgment on quality — spinach, speed limits, and honest referees have all done time as unpopular — so pair it with proof of the count: polls, petitions, empty seats. When the feeling runs hotter than mere dislike, this unit's stronger machinery — despised in the ladder, decried and denounced among the verbs — takes over.
